BatteryLife.title: Battery Life Calculator
BatteryLife.description: Calculation of the battery life of the device from the battery or accumulator
BatteryLife.article:
## Calculation of the battery life of the device from the battery
This calculator provides two options — basic and advanced — to determine the expected battery life of the device. To calculate, you must specify the battery capacity, as well as the current consumed by the device.

CapacitorCode.article:
## Calculation of the nominal value of the capacitor by symbolic marking
The capacitors are marked with numbers and letters that indicate the nominal value of the capacitor. This calculator allows you to calculate the nominal value for various capacitors: film, ceramic, tantalum and mica.

InductorColorCode.title: Inductor Color Code Calculator
InductorColorCode.description: Calculation of the nominal value and tolerance of inductors by color code
InductorColorCode.article:
## Calculation of the nominal inductance by color code
The inductors are marked with colored stripes that indicate the nominal value and tolerance. This calculator allows you to calculate the nominal value and tolerance of inductors. Calculation is supported for inductors with color markings in the form of 4 colored stripes.

LCResonantFrequency.title: Parallel LC Resonant Circuit Calculator
LCResonantFrequency.description: Calculation of the resonant frequency of a parallel LC resonant circuit.
LCResonantFrequency.article:
## Calculation of the resonant frequency of a parallel LC resonant circuit
An LC resonant circuit is a circuit consisting of an inductor and a capacitor that are connected in parallel. When the capacitive and inductive resistances are equal, the circuit has a resonant frequency.
![LC Resonant Frequency Circuit](/images/lc-resonant-frequency-circuit.jpg)

This calculator will help you calculate the third value if you know the other two parameters: inductance, capacitance, or resonant frequency.

The resonant frequency of the circuit is determined by the formula:

$$f = \frac{1}{(2\pi\sqrt{LC})}$$

An oscillatory process occurs in the circuit when the energy of the electric field is converted into the energy of the magnetic field and vice versa. The reactivities of the inductance and capacitance depend on the frequency of the alternating current.

As the frequency increases, the reactance of the inductor increases, and the capacitance decreases. When the frequency decreases, the opposite is true: the inductive resistance decreases, and the capacitive resistance increases.

At a certain frequency, the capacitance of the capacitor becomes equal to the inductive resistance of the coil. This is called current resonance.

The reactivities of the inductor and capacitor can be calculated using the formulas:

$$X_L = 2 \pi f L$$

$$X_C = \frac{1}{(2 \pi f C)}$$

The resonant effect of LC circuits has many important applications in the processing of analog and radio frequency signals. For example, it is used in notch filters, bandpass filters, and generators.

LedResistor.title: LED Resistor Calculator
LedResistor.description: Calculation of a current limiting resistor for one or more LEDs connected in series. This calculator is ideal when you have one or more consecutive LEDs and you need to calculate which resistance resistor needs to be connected to the circuit.
LedResistor.article:
## Calculation of the current limiting resistor for LEDs
![Circuit with LED and resistor](/images/led-resistor-diagram.jpg)

Each LED has a maximum allowable current with which it can operate normally. Even a short-term excess of this maximum current will damage the LED. Thus, it is necessary to limit the current flowing through the LED, one of the ways is to connect a current-limiting resistor in series. It is important to note that this method is not recommended for high-power LEDs that need a full-fledged current regulator.

This calculator allows you to calculate the value of the current limiting resistor, which must be connected in series to the LEDs to limit the current. To do this, enter the specified values. The calculator will also calculate the power dissipated by the resistor, which will help you select the necessary power resistor.
## Calculation formula
$$
R = \frac{V_s - V_{led} * N}{I_{led}}
$$

Where:

$V_s$ – The voltage of the power supply.

$V_{led}$ – Direct voltage. Voltage drop at the p-n junction of the LED.

$I_{led}$ – Forward current. The current at which the LED will work normally will not overheat and the p-n junction will not be broken. For LEDs with a diameter of 3 mm and 5 mm, it is usually 10-30 mA.

$N$ – The number of LEDs connected in series.

The table below shows the approximate values of the voltage drop on LEDs of different colors:

| LED Color | Voltage Drop (V) |
|---|---|
| Infrared | 1.9 |
| Red | 1.6 - 2.03 |
| Orange | 2.03 - 2.1 |
| Yellow | 2.1 - 2.18 |
| Green | 1.9 - 4 |
| Blue | 2.48 - 3.7 |
| Violet | 2.76 - 4 |
| Ultraviolet | 3.1 - 4.4 |

Multivibrator.title: Multivibrator calculator based on NE555
Multivibrator.description: Calculation of the time-consuming components of a multivibrator based on NE555.
Multivibrator.article:
## Calculation of the time-consuming components of a multivibrator
This calculator will help you calculate the frequency and fill factor of the multivibrator signals based on the NE555 timer chip. A circuit for generating rectangular pulses can be built on the basis of the NE555 timer chip. A multivibrator is a relaxation generator that produces a rectangular signal. The word "relaxation" means that the elements that make up the multivibrator do not have the ability to resonate. The figure below shows the NE555-based multivibrator circuit.
![The NE555-based multivibrator circuit](/images/multivibrator-circuit.jpg)
The circuit uses external timing components: $R_A$, $R_B$, $C$, and the amplitude of the output signal is equal to the supply voltage of the chip, which can be 5-12 Volts. The formulas for calculating the signal parameters are presented below:
$$
f = \frac{1}{ln(2) * C * (R_A + 2R_B)}
$$

$$
T_{high} = ln(2) * C * (R_A + R_B)
$$

$$
T_{low} = ln(2) * C * R_B
$$

$$
D = \frac{T_{high}}{T_{low} + T_{high}} = \frac{R_A + R_B}{R_A + 2R_B}
$$

VoltageRegulator.title: Voltage Regulator Calculator
VoltageRegulator.description: Calculation of resistors or voltage for LM317, LM338 or LM350 regulators.
VoltageRegulator.article:
## Calculation of resistors for the voltage regulator
The LM317 voltage regulator requires two external resistors: $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$. They allow you to adjust the output voltage.

![Circuit with LED and resistor](/images/voltage-regulator-diagram.jpg)

This calculator will help you calculate the voltage value for a specific pair of resistors or select a pair of resistors to get the desired voltage. The calculator is suitable for calculating the values of the LM317 controller and some other ICs, such as the LM338 or LM350.

The LM317 is an adjustable voltage regulator that can deliver a current of more than 1.5 A. The output voltage can range from 1.2 V to 37 V, and the input voltage can range from 3 V to 40 V. This regulator is very easy to use and requires only two external resistors to adjust the output voltage.

The output voltage $V_{out}$ depends on the values of external resistors $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ by the following formula:
$$
V_{out} = 1,25 V * (1 + \frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}})
$$

The recommended value of the $R_{1}$ resistor is 240 ohms, but you can also use a different value in the range from 100 ohms to 1000 ohms. To calculate the output voltage of the LM317, enter the value $R_{1}$ and the desired voltage $V_{out}$ in the calculator. For example, if $R_{1}$ is 240 ohms and the desired voltage is 5 V, then the required resistance of resistor $R_{2}$ will be 720 ohms.

OperationalAmplifier.title: Operational Amplifier Calculator
OperationalAmplifier.article:
## Calculation of operational amplifier parameters
This calculator will help you calculate the output voltage and gain values for inverting, non-inverting, and differential switching of an op-amp. To calculate, enter the values of the resistors and input voltage.

An operational amplifier (Op-amp) is a high-gain DC amplifier with a differential input and a single output. The three simplest op-amp switching schemes are inverting, non-inverting, and differential amplifiers. The terms "inverting" and "non-inverting" refer to the polarity of the output voltage relative to the input. The inverting amplifier outputs an output voltage whose polarity is opposite to that of the input voltage. A non-inverting amplifier does not change the polarity of the input voltage.

### Application
Designing with op-amps is much easier than creating individual amplifiers from individual components. The resulting schemas are easily customized to meet the needs of a specific application. The main method of implementing op-amps is to use negative feedback. In typical inverting and non-inverting configurations, the feedback circuit consists of two resistors. The gain of the finished circuit is almost entirely determined by the values of these two resistors.

ParallelEquivalence.title: Parallel Equivalence Calculator
ParallelEquivalence.description: Calculation of the equivalence value of parallel resistors, capacitors and inductors
ParallelEquivalence.article:
## Calculating the equivalence of a parallel connection
This calculator will help you calculate the equivalent nominal of resistors, capacitors, and inductors connected in parallel. For the calculation, select the required element and enter the values.

When connecting capacitors in parallel, their capacitances add up. If you connect resistors or inductors in parallel, their equivalent resistance or inductance, on the contrary, decreases.

Consider, for example, a resistor. If you apply a voltage to it, a certain current will flow through it. By adding another resistor parallel to the first one, you will create a new path for the current. And even if the resistance of the second resistor is large, the total current from the power supply will still be greater than the current through one resistor. And if the total current is greater, then the total equivalent resistance should be less.

### Application
Using multiple parallel resistors allows you to create less effective resistance when there is no resistor with the desired rating. For example, if you need a 1 KOhm resistance and no suitable rating is available, you can use two 2 KOhm resistors connected in parallel.

In addition, the use of parallel resistors also reduces the current passing through each individual resistor in the circuit. This can be useful, for example, when connecting high-power LEDs that consume 500 mW of power. If you use two higher-rated resistors connected in parallel, then only 250 mW will flow through each of them, which will allow you to use standard 0.25 W resistors.

PowerDissipation.title: Power Dissipation Calculator
PowerDissipation.description: Calculation of power dissipation for serial and parallel circuits.
PowerDissipation.article:
## Calculation of power dissipation for serial and parallel circuits
This calculator will help you calculate the power dissipation on resistors in series or parallel connection. For calculation, it is necessary to specify the supply voltage of the circuit and the resistance values of the resistors in the circuit.

SeriesEquivalence.title: Series Equivalence Calculator
SeriesEquivalence.description: Calculation of the equivalence value of series resistors, capacitors and inductors
SeriesEquivalence.article:
## Calculating the equivalence of a series connection
This calculator allows you to calculate the equivalent of series connected resistors, capacitors and inductors. To calculate, select the required element and enter the values.

When connecting resistors and inductors in series, their ratings add up. If you connect series capacitors, their equivalent capacitance, on the contrary, will decrease.

### Application
The use of several series-connected capacitors allows you to increase the total allowable voltage that can be applied to them. For example, if you need to connect a capacitor to a 230 V circuit and no suitable capacitor is available, you can use two 200 V capacitors connected in series, in which case their total allowable voltage will be 400 V.

RCTimeConstant.title: RC Time Constant Calculator
RCTimeConstant.description: Calculation of the time constant (in seconds) of a resistor–capacitor circuit.
RCTimeConstant.article:
## Calculation of the time constant of the RC circuit
The time constant of a serial RC circuit is equal to the product of resistance and capacitance. If two of the three values — resistance, capacitance, or RC time constant-are present, this tool will calculate the missing third variable.

![A series RC charging circuit](/images/rc-time-constant-circuit.jpg)

In an electrical circuit consisting of a capacitance and resistance connected in series, the voltage source $V_S$ is initially isolated from a resistor $R$ and a capacitor $C$ connected in series by an open switch. When the switch is closed, current will flow in the circuit, the capacitor will start charging, and the voltage at its terminals will increase exponentially, and the current flowing in the circuit will decrease exponentially.

### Calculation formula
The charging and discharging rate of successive RC circuits is characterized by the RC time constant, which is denoted by – $\tau$, calculated by the following equation:

$$
\tau = R * C
$$

Where:

$\tau$ – time constant in seconds

$R$ – resistance in ohms

$C$ – capacitance in farads

### Application
RC circuits are widely used as timing elements.

ResistorColorCode.title: Resistor Color Code Calculator
ResistorColorCode.description: Calculation of the nominal value and tolerance of resistors by color code
ResistorColorCode.article:
## Calculation of the nominal value of the resistor by color code
The resistors are marked with colored stripes that indicate the nominal value and tolerance of the resistor. This calculator allows you to calculate the nominal value, tolerance, and temperature coefficient for some resistors. Calculation is supported for color-coded resistors in the form of 4, 5 or 6 color bands.

SmdResistorCode.title: SMD Resistor Code Calculator
SmdResistorCode.description: Calculation of the resistance of an SMD resistor by code
SmdResistorCode.article:
## Calculation of the nominal value of SMD resistors by code
SMD resistors are marked with numbers and letters that indicate the nominal value of the resistor. This calculator allows you to calculate the nominal value for resistors marked with 3 or 4 characters. The EIA-96 marking is also supported.

VoltageDivider.title: Voltage Divider Calculator
VoltageDivider.article:
## Calculation of the voltage divider
A voltage divider is an easy way to get a lower voltage, for this you need to connect two resistors in series and take the voltage between them. To calculate the voltage divider, it is necessary to enter the nominal value of the resistors and the input voltage.

WiresVoltageDrop.title: Wires Voltage Drop Calculator
WiresVoltageDrop.description: Calculation of voltage drop on wires made of various materials of a given length.
WiresVoltageDrop.article:
## Calculation of voltage drop on wires
This calculator will help you calculate the voltage drop on the wires. The tool allows you to select different wire materials: copper, aluminum, gold and others.

ZenerDiode.title: Resistor Calculator for Zener Diode
ZenerDiode.description: Calculation of a resistor for a zener diode.
ZenerDiode.article:
## Calculation of a resistor for a zener diode

This calculator will help you calculate the resistor for a zener diode. For calculation, it is necessary to specify the supply voltage, the zener diode stabilization voltage, the minimum zener diode stabilization current and the current consumed by the load.

The figure below shows a diagram of a simple parametric stabilizer on a zener diode and a resistor.
![Diagram of a parametric voltage stabilizer on a zener diode](/images/zener-diode-circuit.jpg)
A simple parametric stabilizer is based on a semiconductor element known as a zener diode. It operates in the mode of electrical breakdown on the reverse branch of the volt-ampere characteristic, when the supply voltage changes, the current flowing through the zener diode changes, and the voltage on it remains constant.

In order for the zener diode to work correctly, it must be connected in the opposite direction.
